text.en:
Three children lived in three places. Tenzin lived on a mountain, Ravi on a plateau and Lata on a river plain.
Tenzin's family kept yaks and wore thick wool. Ravi's family dug minerals from the rocks. Lata's family grew rice in wide green fields.
"The land shapes how we live," said Lata.

The shapes of the Earth's surface are called landforms. The three main ones are mountains, plateaus and plains.
Mountains are very high and rise steeply. They are cold at the top and have thin air. The Himalayas are the highest mountains in the world.
A plateau is a high flat-topped land with steep sides. It is rich in minerals. The Deccan Plateau is in southern India.
Plains are large flat lands, often near rivers, with fertile soil. Crops grow well and many people live there. The Ganga plain is one of the most populated.
Life depends on landforms. Mountains have fewer people, forests and tourism. Plateaus have mining. Plains have farming, towns and roads.
The shapes on the Earth's surface are landforms: mountains, plateaus and plains.
Mountains are high and steep. The Himalayas are the highest in the world.
A plateau is a high flat land, rich in minerals. The Deccan is a plateau.
Plains are flat and fertile, so crops grow well and many people live there.

problem.en: Why do more people live on plains than on mountains?

text.en: Plains are flat with fertile soil, and rivers bring water.
It is easy to build houses and roads there.

prompt.en: A friend asks why the Deccan region has many mines. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: A plateau is rich in minerals.
The rocks of the Deccan Plateau hold many minerals that people dig out.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking mines are only on mountains.

points.en: Plains are fertile and crowded; plateaus are rich in minerals.
